- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early periods (e.g., 2022-12 to 2023-01), suggesting a persistent upward bias.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, indicating an overshoot after spikes followed by premature mean reversion.
- In periods of high volatility (e.g., 2023-05), model underestimates sharp upward moves, failing to capture sudden spikes.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to true price drops — often forecasting a decline after the market has already turned down.
- Forecasts show diminishing sensitivity to recent low prices; model fails to adjust downward when recent history includes sustained lows.
- In cases where true outcome shows a strong upward trend (e.g., 2023-05), model fails to anticipate the magnitude of the rise, underestimating the peak.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp reversals or sudden drops in price.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (1-2 days) but become more accurate over longer horizons (e.g., 30-day forecasts), suggesting a lag in short-term sensitivity.
